Hi team — attaching the formal runbook for the cutover: borealis_cutover_runbook_v1.pdf (attachment). High-level summary below and key callouts for the implementation window.

1) Provisioning steps (timeline estimates):
  - Create reserved GPU pool (4x A100-80GB nodes) — ~30 min
  - Network validation & VPC peering test — ~20 min
  - Model artifact pull & warm-up (prefix caching) — ~45 min
  - Autoscale policy attach and dry-run (no traffic) — ~15 min
  - Controlled traffic ramp (staged lanes) — ~60 min

2) Autoscale & burst policy recommendations (production):
  - Target concurrency per node: 12 concurrent sessions
  - Scale-out threshold: 70% sustained utilization over 60s
  - Burst buffer: reserve 1.5x normal headroom; configured as a burst pool with billing meter for burst usage
  - Warm standby region: us-west (hot-warm), replicate KV-cache metadata; failover test included in post-cutover validation

3) Rollback & safety nets:
  - Fast rollback: detach dedicated pool routing and fail back to hosted API (traffic-splitting)
  - Data safety: no customer stored PII is migrated during cutover; model artifacts are pulled from the customer's secure repo over mTLS
  - Monitoring: preconfigured dashboards for token-level latency and cost; alerts at 10% higher-than-baseline error rate

4) Cost estimate for burst capacity (attached): estimated_burst_costs.csv — includes per-hour and monthly projections for 2x and 3x burst demand.

Pre-cutover checklist (please complete 24h before window):
- Confirm VPC peering + allowlist (network contact reply OK)
- Provide test service account (we'll return an expiring API key)
- Confirm SRE contact and Slack channel for real-time updates

Drive link for collaborative edits: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-cutover-borealis

I'll be on the cutover as implementation lead; Monica will handle verification and performance tuning after ramp.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marcus — short answers, with links to appendices in the runbook: 

1) Burst costs: see estimated_burst_costs.csv (attached). For a sustained 2x baseline over a 90-day rolling window we estimate an incremental cost of ~USD 42k — this assumes our burst metering and a 1.5x headroom policy. We can run a model-specific projection if you share typical token rates.

2) RPO/RTO for warm-standby (us-west):
  - RPO: ~15 minutes for KV-cache metadata (periodic sync + async replication)
  - RTO: ~6–9 minutes for traffic cutover using our automated routing and warm caches (dependent on model warming)

If you need tighter RTOs we can increase pre-warmed capacity in us-west, but that changes reserved capacity and cost.

Marissa
